themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. A shared standard or a central system cannot settle a fight over money, credit, or turf.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic all three models say agents profit by pretending to be human and that several parties benefit from the ambiguity, while the semantic context layer answers call conflicting definitions a political settlement, journey orchestration answers say channel owners are paid to say yes, and incrementality answers note platforms have no reason to expose how treatment was assigned.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and the thing you measure often shifts while you measure it. So the usual first move is to build a small truth set of your own, or admit you are only estimating.
themes.evidence: Today's agentic traffic answers all start by manufacturing labeled agent sessions from payment events or recruited pilots, echoing answer engine optimization (no stable unit or denominator), identity resolution (no natural signal that a link was wrong), and B2B buying-group signal (a degraded signal and a fake one look identical).

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and force everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Safe agent execution answers all propose a proxy or control plane holding the credentials and hard caps on spend, rate, and audience size, and the same shape appears as one egress gate for consent enforcement, one pre-send eligibility check for journey orchestration, and a dedicated signed endpoint for agent traffic.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, money, or a message leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. Compliance and effects can only be estimated from outside, never proven.
themes.evidence: Downstream consent answers agree that enforcement ends where your systems end and that walled gardens and trained models expose no lineage or deletion evidence, and agent traffic answers add that the person the agent acts for is never present on the wire to verify.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls depend on meaning, context, and what a sentence implies, and no rule set fully captures that. The models end up shrinking human judgment into a smaller, safer box rather than removing it.
themes.evidence: Generative content governance answers converge on an approved-claims library plus limits on what models may say because deciding whether wording is supported is a reasoning task, and semantic context layer answers say context-dependent meaning cannot be flattened into one global definition.
